The Advisor's three owner items (#2257 items 6, 7 and 8), plus the Advisor's
share of the deep-link class (#2253). Part of #2257 and part of #2253. The
roster's `fixes` is empty for this group, so the orchestrator closes them
after verifying each.

What the owner's screenshot (2026-10-14) named, and what answers it:

- **Item 8: "A degree warmer costs -266 SEK/month more" beside "a degree
  cooler is cheaper ≈ 140".** Two defects stacked.
  1. The degree tiles moved `target_temp` alone. The plan heats to the comfort
     schedule (`comfort_temp_day`/`_night`), so a tile priced only what
     `target_temp` still reaches (the settlement caps and the terminal value),
     not a degree of comfort.
  2. The figure was the plan's single-solve spend difference from the house
     as it stands, scaled to a month. A degree cooler books a one-off coast,
     a degree warmer a one-off heat-up, and the scaling multiplied each by
     every horizon in the month.

  The fix:
  - A degree tile now moves every comfort level the schedule has set: target,
    day, night, and the weekend and holiday overrides where they are set.
  - It reads the thermostat baseline's difference, `monthly_held_cost_delta`.
    That is a degree held from a steady start, which the SAV-BASELINE
    settlement already starts held.
  - The card checks the pair before rendering it: a degree cooler must save
    and a degree warmer must cost, in the whole units the row renders. A pair
    out of that order renders as "Not shown yet", with no money and no
    "costs … more" sentence. A degree cooler that saves nothing (no heating)
    is no row.
- **Item 6: the "worth doing" figures swing day to day.** Every tile is
  published as the mean of its daily means over the last 30 local days
  (`price_tiles.HORIZON_DAYS`), with `horizon_days` beside it. The days
  persist with the ledger, so a restart does not start the mean over. The
  degree row says it is "a 30-day average".
- **Item 7: "Open settings" does not deep-link (R10-DEEPLINK's helper).**
  Home Assistant has no URL into a single options-flow step (R10-DEEPLINK's
  carry). So each enable-to-see row, and the feedback-sensor row, now names
  the step that turns it on, for example "Configure → Savings vs comfort" for
  the price of a degree. The button opens this entry through
  `openHaLink(host, "options")`, dispatched by a new `open_options` act; the
  Health page keeps `settings`, which R10-UX-HEALTH converts.
- **Carried from R10-SAV-REASONS:** `REASON_LABELS` and the card's
  `reasons.*` strings now name `boost`, `comfort_mode`,
  `system_identification` and `untagged`, so the Savings receipt's by-reason
  bars stop printing the raw token. A census reads `payload.py`'s `REASON_`
  constants and refuses any code that has no label.

**The check is order, not convexity: a decision for the owner to confirm.**
The roster brief asks for "a convexity and monotonicity check across -1, 0
and +1 degC". Round 1 rendered the pair only if the warmer degree cost at
least what the cooler one saved, within one rounding unit. Review B1 showed
that this hides correct rows in production, and this round measured why
(Figures, `rotation`):

- **The estimator gives convexity no margin.** The thermostat's COP does not
  depend on its target, so its cost is linear in the target. The only
  departures are the horizon's unsettled end state and how many 15-minute
  steps a coast lasts. Both are a few per cent of the figure, of either sign,
  and depend on the start time.
- **Production samples the two tiles apart.** It prices one tile per
  scheduled solve, in rotation, so the two means come from different solves.
  At the harness's 40 days, the published gap (warmer + cooler) spans
  -2.29..+0.55 at 30 min, -1.82..+1.22 at 60 and -2.50..+2.06 at 120.
- **Result:** the convexity check hid the row on 14, 3 and 30 of 40 evenings,
  which is the reviewer's own count.

Monotonicity is what the held figure keeps at every start. A mean of
same-signed samples keeps the sign, so no sampling can break the order
check. The order check alone still refuses the screenshot's pair.

Alternatives considered:
- **Pricing both degree tiles from the same solve.** This removes only the
  sampling half. The reviewer's `both-every-solve` control is still concave
  by up to 2.3 on 11 of 40 days.
- **A tolerance sized to the measured gap.** That is a threshold fitted to
  one house and one cadence.
- **A convex estimator.** It would need the COP to depend on the target in
  the thermostat model, which is a physics change outside this seam.

So the convexity half of the brief's sentence is not built. If the owner
wants it, it needs one of those three changes, not this check.

**Why the held figure, and not the alternatives.**
1. The plan's own single-solve delta with the schedule moved overstates the
   price. The `null` arm reads +145.6 and +85.1 per degree, against a
   realised +59.4.
2. Settling each plan's stored heat against its own thermostat
   (`predicted_cost + deferred_energy_cost`, the SAV-BASELINE figures) is
   honest for one plan but not across two schedules, because each side is
   settled against a different thermostat.
3. Settling the two plans' end states against each other at the refill price
   read wrong signs in round 1's scratch probe. Neither 2 nor 3 is used, and
   no figure from either is claimed.

The held figure is monotone at every start this round measured. Concretely:
- every one of the 40 midnight days;
- every published evening at 30, 60 and 120 min;
- the real seam, at a night and an afternoon instant.

In the null it reads the plan's realised price per degree within 8.4 %. It
does not depend on the live house: a coasted (19 °C) and a pre-heated
(23 °C) house price a degree identically. That is the property the plan's
single-solve figure lacked.

**Architecture.** The tiles' state, perturbation set, sampling, horizon and
persistence moved out of the coordinator class into a new pure module,
`price_tiles.py`. Its per-coordinator side table holds the book
(`boost.py`'s discipline), and the coordinator hands the functions the book,
never itself. `_price_tile_specs` and the `_price_tiles` attribute are gone,
and their seam map entry is removed. This round changes no production line
outside the card's `degreeRow`.

**Review B2 (MB5 killed only at some hours).** The real-seam check now runs
at two fixed instants (03:07 and 15:07 UTC, `_fi_dt.freeze`), from a house at
19 °C and at 23 °C. It requires the held figures to be equal across the two
starts, and the plan's single-solve figures to differ by more than 1.0.
MB5 (the held figure read from `predicted_cost`) now fails on the clock the
check fixes, not on the wall clock. The reviewer's MX1 (the save side of the
ledger) is now pinned too.

MB5 is killed at a clock the check fixes. The check freezes 03:07 and 15:07

## Null control

- **The unmutated tree passes.** `python3 tests/features.py` →
  `ALL 4282 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, and `node tests/card.mjs` →
  `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED` (Figures).
- **The seam check's own null.** Under a probe that only falsifies the
  assertion (no production line touched), the detail prints the unmutated
  figures:
  - held: -31.27 / +31.27 at 03:07 and -37.98 / +38.01 at 15:07, identical for
    the 19 °C and 23 °C house;
  - the plan's single-solve figures: -116.07 / +140.78 against -114.95 /
    +138.63 at 03:07, and -126.08 / +84.77 against -78.35 / +56.40 at 15:07.

  So the "they differ" half has a margin at both instants, and the "they are
  equal" half is exact.
- **The rotation arm's null: a flat price and a constant outdoor
  temperature**, at the default 30 min. 40 of 40 evenings shown at the base
  and at the head, gap +0.38 every evening. This is the case where nothing
  can go wrong; had the arm read a hidden evening here, the instrument would
  be broken, not the card.
- **The rotation arm's precondition** is asserted, not assumed. At three
  starts (00:00, 07:00, 13:00) the stubbed solver's held figure equals the
  real solver's exactly: `[67.9, 80.02, 74.03]` both. The arm refuses itself
  (`VERDICT rotation INVALID`) otherwise.
- **The owner's null (carry 1, and SAV-BASELINE's restatement): a flat price
  and a constant outdoor temperature.** Here the plan has no timing to buy.
  - `r10_advisor_degree.py null` reads +59.4 per delivered degree realised on
    both sides, against the held +54.4 (-8.4 %, within the harness's 15 %
    bound for the loop's own stored-heat settlement).
  - The plan's first-solve figures read +145.6 and +85.1: the transient the
    merge base published.
- **The varying-outdoor arm (`timing`)** separates timing.
  - With the outdoor swing the plan buys in warmer hours, and its realised
    cost per delivered degree reads +1.3 and +40.8 against the held +54.7.
  - At three days this arm is too noisy to read as a term. It shows the plan
    at or below the held figure; it is not a number for the gain.
- **The merge base's tile on the same 40 days** (`days` arm, base column):
  non-monotone on 5 of 40 days, and no effect at all (0 / 0) on 3.

**How the horizon removes the noise (carry 2), with those numbers.**
- What moves day to day is that day's weather and prices: std 29.6.
- The published figure is the mean of 30 daily means, so one day moves it by
  a thirtieth. Over days 30–40 its std is 1.1.
- Independent days would give 29.6 / √30 ≈ 5.4. The synthetic sequence is
  periodic (7 price days, a 9-day weather swing), so its 30-day windows nearly
  coincide, and the measured 1.1 is lower than real weather would give. The
  5.4 is the rule's figure, not a measurement.

**`null`:**
- `RESULT null offset -1 delivered -0.514 K truth_per_delivered_degree +59.4 held +54.4 (-8.4 %) first_solve_plan +145.6`
- `RESULT null offset +1 delivered +0.327 K truth_per_delivered_degree +59.4 held +54.4 (-8.4 %) first_solve_plan +85.1`
- `VERDICT null held figure within 15 % …`

The plan delivers only -0.514 K and +0.327 K per degree of setting here.
So the tile, which prices a degree held, overstates what moving the setting
saves by roughly 1.8× and 3×. Whether "a degree cooler ≈ 54" is the right copy
for a button that moves the setting is round 1's open question for the judge
or owner. It is unchanged here.

Contract: `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` from origin/main (`git diff merge-base...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the copy is current).

## Blocking

### B1. Step 6, configuration attack: under production's sampling the card hides the row it is meant to fix

`price_tiles` refreshes ONE tile per scheduled solve (`_maybe_refresh_price_tile`, cursor over 3 specs). So `target_minus_1` and `target_plus_1` are sampled from different solves, at different start times, and averaged separately. The card then renders the pair only if `cost >= save - 1` (convex within one rounding unit), which assumes the two published means are exactly antisymmetric.
The body backs that assumption with the `days` arm: "the two tiles are antisymmetric within 0.9 every day". But that arm prices both tiles from the SAME solve, always at 00:00. It also counts only sign monotonicity (`cooler < 0 < warmer`), never the card's `degreeRow` predicate.

The reviewer-built probe (`ev/tools/rotation_probe.py`; disclosed as mine, not the finder's or the fixer's) replays production instead:
- the harness's own house and its 40-day price and weather sequence, concatenated;
- one tile per solve in rotation, at a fixed cadence;
- `price_tiles.record` / `published`, and the card's predicate applied each local evening.

The solver is stubbed because `baseline_cost` (the thermostat's) does not depend on it. `ev/probe_stub_fidelity.txt` shows the real and stub figures are identical to 4 decimals at 3 intraday starts.

```
RESULT rotation cadence 30 min: card NOT shown on 14/40 days (2/11 from day 30); asym (up+down) range -2.29..+0.55
RESULT rotation cadence 60 min: card NOT shown on 3/40 days (0/11 from day 30); asym (up+down) range -1.82..+1.22
RESULT rotation cadence 90 min: card NOT shown on 12/40 days (0/11 from day 30); asym (up+down) range -3.01..+0.14
RESULT rotation cadence 120 min: card NOT shown on 30/40 days (10/11 from day 30); asym (up+down) range -2.50..+2.06
RESULT both-every-solve cadence 30 min: card NOT shown on 11/40 days (1/11 from day 30); asym (up+down) range -2.30..+0.40
RESULT both-every-solve cadence 120 min: card NOT shown on 3/40 days (0/11 from day 30); asym (up+down) range -1.92..+0.17
```

Example (30 min, day 39): published −77.64 / +76.40. That is monotone and correctly signed. The card still renders "Not shown yet: … did not price in the order heating does".

Two causes, both open:
1. **The held estimator is not convex across intraday starts.** In the `both-every-solve` control, both tiles come from every solve, and it is still concave by up to 2.3/month on 11 of 40 days. Midnight-only sampling hides this.
2. **The rotation adds sampling asymmetry.** At 120 min it rises from 3/40 to 30/40.

`optimization_interval` is a user setting (10–120 min, default 30, `config_flow.py:1730`). So the PR's premise ("heat loss grows with the gap, so comfort's cost is convex … within the one unit two roundings open") fails at the default setting, on the fixer's own house. Item 8 then shows up as a hidden row instead of a contradictory one.

A fix has to make the render check agree with what the estimator and its sampling can actually guarantee. Options include pairing the two degree tiles in one turn, a tolerance derived from the measured asymmetry, or checking only the sign. The harness also needs an arm that samples like production and applies the card's predicate.

### B2. Step 1, mutation proof: MB5 does not reproduce, because its only killer depends on the clock

The body lists MB5 (`monthly_held_cost_delta` from `predicted_cost`) as killed by "#2257: at the real what-if seam …". The body itself says `_solve_coord` anchors on the real clock.
At this head, with the same replacement, `python3 tests/features.py` → `ALL 4276 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (rc 0) at 15:53 UTC, and again at 16:09 UTC (`ev/mut_MB5_rerun_features.log`). The seam check printed the plan's figures under the mutant, `(-63.76, 97.70)`; they satisfy `down < 0 < up` and `up + down >= -1`.
So the one line that makes the tile read the held figure, rather than the transient the owner complained about, is pinned only at some times of day. A reviewer at another hour would see it killed, which is how the body recorded it. A clock-independent check is owed: for example a fixed start, or a seam case where the plan's single-solve delta is non-monotone and the held one is not.

## Non-blocking findings (fold into the re-cut)

- **MX1 (reviewer's mutant) survives.** Deleting `"price_tiles": price_tiles.book(self),` from `_schedule_ledger_save` passes `tests/features.py` (4276) and `tests/finite_boundary.py` (rc 0). So the body's claim that "the days persist with the ledger, so a restart does not start the mean over" is not pinned on its save side.
